attribute: An understanding of God, a personal faith in Jesus Christ as Saviour and Lord, and the capacity to articulate this contextually;
beginning: Is open to the love of God, discipleship of Christ and the inspiration of the Holy Spirit within their life.
Speaks confidently about their experience as a person of Christian faith.
developing: Understands that there are a variety of experiences and faith expressions of Christian identity.
Appreciates that the conversation partner may express faith using different language and from different life experience.
Explores various models and images of God, salvation and Trinity.
established: Seeks to understand the other in the conversation both culturally and linguistically.
Articulates their faith with discernment, personal insight and self-awareness in conversation with the listener.
Demonstrates personal resilience in faith.
lfd: LFD 1: Faith Sharing: Public speaking; 2 min Homily; Faith sharing - word and deed; Why I follow Jesus. Key educational units: Beginning with Jesus Doctrines of Salvation God the Trinity Integrative Ministry Practice SFE Statements of faith – mid-course review and transition interview

attribute: The practice of Christian spiritual disciplines and embodying faith in Jesus Christ in their own lives.
beginning: Aware of the importance of applying Christian virtues in everyday life.
Habits of reading the Bible and prayer are established, using a range of resources.
Understands that engaging with the scriptures is essential to vital spiritual life.
developing: Explores and experiences a variety of spiritual disciplines.
Understands the importance of the history of spiritual disciplines and their relevance for contemporary life.
established: Established habits that explore and participate in spiritual disciplines.
Reflects theologically on their lived experience and applies it to daily life.
Confident to lead others in the practice of spiritual disciplines.
lfd: LFD 2: Supervision, Spiritual Direction, Mentor, Coach, Counsellor and Psychologist. What are they? What do each bring? Benefits of each? Always seeking to have a balance in life. Also: Spiritual Direction (at least 6 sessions), Professional Supervision, Mentor, annual spiritual retreats, emphasis on Prayer Key educational units: Introduction to Christian Spirituality and Discipleship Reflective Ministry Practice

attribute: Acknowledging a call by God through the Church to give themselves to the Ministry for which they are ordained, following Jesus’ pattern of love and service;
beginning: Articulates their experience of call.
Understands that their call must be recognised by the Church for ordination.
Acknowledges the discipline of the church in oversight.
Awareness of the different ministries in the Uniting Church.
developing: Sense of call is strengthened and tested in study, and formation.
Clarity of call develops with openness to new directions and possibilities.
Prepares for ministry with perseverance, resilience, imaginative wisdom and integrity.
established: Ongoing discernment of call, which is tested and confirmed by the church.
The individual lives their sense of call through showing appropriate Christian values of love, acting justly and in service with humility.
Demonstrates the gifts and graces for Ministry in their chosen contexts which is embodied through ‘cruciform’ patterns of ministry and service.
lfd: LFD 3. Ordination Distinctive: Deacon focus and stories; MoW focus and stories; Solid understanding of Theology of ordination; Distinctions between the different ministries in UCA eg MoP; Wider responsibility for church; A minister amongst a community of ministers. LFD 4. Future shape of ministry: Lifelong ordination; the cost of sacrificial service; “order” of ministry; Bi-vocational; Ministry from the margins. Key educational units: The Practice of Christian Ministry Heritage, Theology and Polity of the UCA, Capstone on reflective Practice.

attribute: A mature knowledge of the Christian tradition and the biblical witness, and the ability to help the Church shape its future in the light of that tradition;
beginning: Personal study and contemplation of the Bible resulting in biblical literacy and resonance.
Acknowledging that all members of the church have a voice in shaping its future.
Awareness of issues affecting contemporary society and church life.
developing: Critically engages in biblical study using traditional and contemporary approaches.
Writes and speaks about the theological and exegetical process in depth.
Applies study to personal and church life through reflection and action.
established: Reflects carefully upon the biblical text for current context and listens carefully to alternative voices.
Leads others in a reasoned interpretation of the biblical text and Christian tradition in writing and speaking, and visual formats.
Applies the text appropriately to the contemporary context of ministry.
Able to use biblical texts for imaginative reading and contemplative practices.
lfd: LFD5: State of the church in Australia and Globally; World Christianity – theology and our place in it. LFD 6: Church and its future, With reference to Church History and our current context (LFD5); LFD 7: Public Theology, missional calling; local theologising; place of agencies and specialised Christian ministries. Key educational units: Four field B (Biblical) and Four field C (Theology) units; Biblical Hermeneutics for Mission and Ministry

attribute: A capacity to articulate Christian faith in contextually appropriate ways;
beginning: Understands that faith needs both well reasoned belief and a vibrant spiritual life.
Willingness to engage in developing appropriate responses to questions with other people’s input and perspectives.
developing: Explores and studies apologetics on the Christian faith.
Demonstrates an understanding of different models of evangelism.
Communicates the faith in a variety of ways.
Practises the skills of good questions and reflective listening.
Acts upon their understanding of social and ecological issues.
Continuing openness to new expressions of Christian living.
established: Confidently engages with questions about Christian faith.
Speaks about Christian faith appropriately to the listener and responds with cultural sensitivity and authenticity.
Able to communicate the gospel within their personal story, the story of the church and that of the listeners.
Demonstrates engagement with ecumenical and other faith traditions in a thoughtful and sensitive way.
lfd: LFD 8: Scenarios and guest presentations from a number of ministry contexts. Key educational units: Introduction to Christian Mission Homiletics

attribute: Adherence to the Basis of Union (BoU);
beginning: Introduced to the BoU as a foundational document of the UCA.
Awareness of the formation of the UCA, its ethos, and its traditions.
Commitment to working in partnership with the ministry of women and men.
developing: Is immersed into an understanding of the BoU and other foundational documents of the UCA and seeks to apply them to church life and ministry.
Interrogates the BoU, its strengths and limitations.
Engages with the creeds named in the BoU.
established: Commitment to the BoU and its ethos of UCA at ordination.
Can readily access, understand and respond to UCA documents that shape a distinctively ‘Uniting’ approach to ministry.
Intentionally shares an understanding and vision of Basis of Union with others.
lfd: LFD 9: Introduction to the BoU with an emphasis on its understanding of ministry and the role of the minister. Key educational units: Heritage, Theology and Polity of the UCA Church History A & B Other ministry subjects like Church, Ministry and Sacraments

attribute: Being equipped to help the Church be faithful to its identity and lead the Church in mission in a rapidly changing and diverse cultural and social context;
beginning: Awareness of the scope of the post Christian era and its impact.
Clear commitment to working with the Church on the quest for fresh expressions of life and ministry.
Awareness of living in a multi faith society.
developing: Demonstrates an understanding of the history of missions.
Engages in missional thinking in general and in specific contexts.
Experiments with new methods of ministry.
Explores whether they may be able to regenerate or plant new expressions of ministry for a new generation.
Engaging in interfaith dialogue and with those who practise other spiritualities.
established: Integrates an understanding of new cultural contexts into their ministry.
Recognises the need for change, to innovate, regenerate, or let go of ministry methods which no longer function effectively.
Demonstrates skills in flexible ministry development, community engagement and outreach, and chaplaincy.
Demonstrates confidence to engage in public ministry.
lfd: LFD 10: Suspend judgement, Living with difference; Christ and culture; Secularism. LFD 11: Space for Grace, Exclusion and Embrace. LFD 12: Social Media: influencer; identity; reflection; emerging tech. Also: Overseas cross cultural immersion with partner church, Rural Field trip, Remote Aboriginal Community trip, Global City experience, Frontier services, Chaplaincy including prison Key educational units: Reading Cultures Introduction to Christian Mission Introduction to Christian Leadership Theology of Leadership

attribute: Commitment to the Covenant with the Uniting Aboriginal and Islander Christian Congress (1994) and working within the understandings expressed in the Preamble to the Constitution (2009);
beginning: Awareness that the UCA is in covenant relationship with Uniting Aboriginal and Islander Christian Congress (UAICC).
Displays a sensitivity to the cultural gap between First and Second peoples.
Demonstrates understanding of the complexities surrounding racism and colonialism.
developing: Studies texts on indigenous history including impact of colonialism, invasion, and the frontier wars.
Explores the Preamble to the constitution in study and discussion.
Has and reflects upon an immersion experience with UAICC or an indigenous community.
Reflects upon the questions of covenant, justice and reconciliation with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people.
established: Working with others to develop and put in place a reconciliation or covenanting action plan
Acts appropriately in their commitment to relationships with UAICC and others first nations people and groups.
Demonstrates reconciliation and continued working together in partnership.
lfd: LFD 13: Intro to Congress - covenant, and preamble lead by congress leaders; LFD 14: Reading some wider resources and engaging with them in conversation with Congress members. Eg sovereignty or Uluru statement Also: Walk on Country immersion experience offered each year - Adnyamathanha; Kaurna; Ngarrindjeri; Remote Aboriginal Community trip; other seminars and learning contexts. Key educational units: UD unit: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Approaches to Christian theology [Decolonizing Service]

attribute: Embodying the Church’s declarations that We Are A Multicultural Church (1985), Living with the Neighbour Who is Different (2000), and One Body Many Members, Living faith and life cross culturally (2012)
beginning: Understands that the UCA is a multi-cultural church in which we all participate.
Willingness to engage in discussions with those who are culturally different to ourselves.
Recognises that culture is evolving and dynamic.
Demonstrates an understanding of the documents of the UCA regarding intercultural life together.
developing: Demonstrates and articulates an in-depth understanding of their own culture and its presumptions.
Explores cultural differences by engaging in intercultural conversations and worship.
Develops awareness and care for those on the margins in a range of contexts.
Has an appreciation of the refugee experience and the challenges of migration.
Explores the ways intercultural and contextual theology impacts on ministry.
established: Prepared to work in collaboration with diverse congregations building a climate of co-operation.
Continues to deepen their study of culture and is able to integrate intercultural readings of text and culture into their own theological framework and expression of ministry.
Commitment to work with people living on the margins by creating space for listening and dialogue, and finding ways of walking together in ministry.
lfd: LFD 15: Intro to the UCA Documents and UCA context nationally and in SA; Awareness of the Intercultural mapping in SA project. LFD 16: Focus on CQ with Paul Goh and David Turnbull Also: Building Bridges; 1 on 1 or group intercultural supervision; 1 month placement in an intercultural community for contextual learning; or with a specific ethnic community organisation; Quarterly forum as participant/observer; make intercultural friendships. Key educational units: Reading Cultures

attribute: A well-developed and reflective understanding of their identity as an ordained Minister within the Uniting Church;
beginning: Understands the process and requirements for ordination.
Demonstrates a readiness to undertake formation for ministry.
Has a history of ministry engagement.
developing: Explores documents of the UCA on ordination and standards for ministry.
Expresses theological understanding of ministry consonant with UCA polity.
Compares UCA ordination with that of other denominations.
Encountering other ministry agents engaged in different forms of ministry.
established: Commitment to maintaining standards of professionalism and integrity as a minister of the UCA.
Is self-disciplined about work-life balance and displays appropriate patterns of self-care.
Can reflect upon their journey in ministry in contextually appropriate language.
Commitment to submit to the discipline of the UCA.
Demonstrate familiarity with the polity and governance of the Uniting Church and their responsibilities as ordained ministers.
lfd: LFD 17: Going the distance in ministry: Resilience; Mental health; Maturity; Emotional intelligence; Knowing yourself; Burnout; Fatigue; Stress; Self- care; Receive feedback constructively; Non-anxious presence in ministry. Key educational units: Introduction to Pastoral Care Caring Practices of the Church

attribute: Ability to engage the tasks of Ministry with critical imagination, courage, emotional maturity, theological judgment and self-reflection; and to exercise this Ministry within the ministry of the whole people of God;
beginning: Exhibits self-awareness of their own traits of critical imagination, courage, emotional maturity, theological judgment and self-reflection, and areas of growth.
Ability to identify and name areas of growth to develop into ordained ministry with the whole people of God.
developing: Demonstrates these traits of critical imagination, courage, emotional maturity, theological judgment and self-reflection in all aspects of the formation programme.

Presentations of ministry reflections, displays ability to self-reflect and use theological judgement, and how critical imagination courage and emotional maturity are used in their field education and other ministry opportunities.
Displays courage and insight in self-awareness within relationships and corresponding adaptability.
Expresses ability to discern the parameters of relationships and what working with others requires in their growth.
Displays understanding of issues of leadership and collaboration, people skills, and group dynamics.
established: Synthesizes skills in teaching and forming people of all ages for a life of discipleship.
Demonstrates the exercise of pastoral ministry including in relation to grief, trauma, personal crises, and when to refer to professional help
Shows leadership ability in developing planning and shared ministry
lfd: LFD 18: Imagination, courage, and self-reflection in ministry. LFD 19: Enneagram – a pathway to knowing yourself better. Key educational units: CPE Integrative Ministry Practice Reflective Ministry Practice.

attribute: Readiness for the practice of day-to-day Ministry, and the quality of being and awareness which gives integrity to the exercise of this practice;
beginning: Has basic skills for worship leadership.
Has ability to undertake pastoral care.
Can read the community culture and recognise elements of community ministry.
developing: Leadership of worship and preaching, displays understandings of theology and complexity.
Can evaluate elements of pastoral care undertaken and areas of strength and growth.
Engaging with NCLS and census data, is able to study a community environment and plan with others for community engagement.
Grasps the basic management skills required in administration, finance and budgeting, and building management.
Enables others who may have complementary skills to themselves.
established: Displays gifts for ministry in areas such as preaching, worship leadership, planning and collaborating on strategic plans with the people of God.
Articulates their own ministry identity with reference to recent examples.
Recognises their own gifting and how they are prepared to use them in ministry.
Creates and collaborates in preparation and leadership of worship in liturgy and preaching appropriate for the context.
Exhibits abilities to engage in pastoral care in congregational and community settings
Prepared for pastoral and worship functions of marriage, funerals, baptisms, and sacraments.
Evidence of the ability to help groups move toward new ways of being God’s people in the world.
Ability to negotiate and resolve conflict situations constructively.
lfd: LFD 20: Developing a toolbox: Budget/finance; Time management; Self-presentation; Conflict management; Staff/HR; Managing people; “Craft and Inner disposition” of a minister. - Jonathan Davies, Sean Gilbert. LFD 21: Weddings, Funerals and other rites of passage. - Ann Hewitt, David Hoffman, Jenni Hughes, and Sean Gilbert. Key educational units: Liturgy and Worship Church Ministry and Sacraments

attribute: The capacity for and commitment to intentional life-long learning;
beginning: Displays a willingness for working in ministry reflection.
Integration of prior learning into formation.
developing: Engages in intensive study during Phase 2.
Understands that a number of skills will be developed in Phase 3 and 4.
Demonstrates ongoing learning within supervision in Field Education.
established: Engages willingly in learning new skills for ministry. Demonstrates the ability to develop a plan for their own learning. Has an ongoing learning plan that informs study and learning undertaken.
lfd: LFD 22: How to read; What to read; Why learning matters and strategies; How to learn; Academic future; Thinking short and Long; Compost: How do I know what I need to know? Also: Formation journaling throughout time as a candidate

attribute: Commitment to comply with the Code of Ethics and Ministry Practice.
beginning: Awareness of Code of Ethics (CoE) and familiar with contents of the various codes for lay and ordained persons.
Completes CoE intro, and Safe Church training.
developing: Understands the context in which CoE has arisen and the requirement to adhere to the CoE in ministry practice.
Attends workshops on ethical ministry.
Awareness of living in the discipline of the Church.
established: Demonstrated commitment to Code of Ethics, and other professional standards of ministry practice.
Demonstrated integrity to grow in response to CoE, and those which may yet develop around ethical ministry.
lfd: LFD 23: Dealing with “Heavy Stuff” in community – Domestic violence/abuse; Coercive control; Euthanasia; bioethics. LFD 24: How to minister in a politically diverse environment; How to lead and minister in a theologically diverse church; Conflict; Collegiality; Beyond tribalism. Stories of diverse communities thriving. Also: Called to Care (1/2 day), Through Their Eyes (1 day), Mental Health First aid (2 day course), Code of Ethics course (2 day Course), Conflict training (2 day course) Key educational units: [Introduction to Developmental Psychology] [Introduction to Human Social Development] SFE
